animations._comment: Opening animation modes. 'id' becomes the `data-animation` attribute of <html>/<body> and therefore selects the flavour declared in css/animations/; 'labelKey' is the translation of the picker button; 'parodic' flags a mode that is deliberately ridiculous (the settings screen advertises it); 'tearMs'/'flipMs'/'staggerMs' are the durations in milliseconds (opening of the pack, one card flip, delay between two summary cards) applied through the `--anim-tear-ms`/`--anim-flip-ms`/`--anim-stagger-ms` custom properties, so a mode only needs numbers here. 'normal' is the cinematic base (see css/components/card-reveal.css and css/views/opening.css), 'epic' stages it (light rays, shockwave, motes) and 'explosive' is the joke one (confetti, stickers, shake). A mode declared without a matching CSS block simply reuses the base animation at its own speed. The Mine Pick reads the very same durations.

foil._comment: Strength of the foil of the super rare, legendary and mythic printings, as a percentage of the intensity it was designed at. The four values bound the first slider of the settings screen; 'min' at 0 switches the foil off completely (the planes become transparent and their animation is stopped), and 'default' is what a new account starts at and what a player who never opens the slider keeps seeing. js/utils/FoilManager.js publishes the value as `--foil-intensity` (a 0-1 factor) on <html>, which css/components/card-shine.css multiplies into the opacity of its planes. A value outside the range is CLAMPED, never rejected: narrowing the range later must stay safe for saves written with a wider one.

glare._comment: Strength of the SECOND slider of the foil panel ('Brillance'): the bright line that sweeps across the artwork, back and forth, on top of the foil's shapes. It has its own range and its own preference because the two effects are independent - a player can keep the honeycomb and the embossing while muting the moving line, or the other way round. FoilManager publishes it as `--glare-intensity` (a 0-1 factor) on <html>; the line is drawn by the `.card-shine__gleam` layer. Same clamping rule as the foil above.

notifications._comment: Game notifications (the queue at the top of the screen: collection progress, experience earned, a player title unlocked). 'duration' bounds the slider that decides how many SECONDS one notification stays on screen, 'default' is what a new account starts at; 'types' lists the kinds the player can switch off in the settings (a disabled kind is dropped by `NotificationCenter.push`). The values live per account in `user_state["settings"].notificationDuration` and `.notificationTypes`. These are NOT the action toasts of the bottom of the screen: those keep their own short life.

glow._comment: Glow ('Illumination') ranges. Each effect has its own 0-N slider on the settings screen, so a future one never inherits the bounds of another: 'trophies' is the halo around a trophy medal (none for bronze, light for silver and gold, medium for diamond and emerald - see css/components/trophy.css), and a 'cards' block will be added here when the card glow is tuned. The intensity is stored per account in `user_state["settings"].glowTrophies`; `js/utils/GlowManager.js` publishes it as the 0-N factor `--trophy-glow-scale` on <html>, which the stylesheets multiply into the radius of their shadows. 0 switches the effect off completely.

boosters._comment: 'extraBoosterPriceSparks' is the price of ONE extra daily booster, bought with Sparks once the free daily boosters ('dailyFreeBoosters') are all spent. A bought booster is kept in the quota under its own bucket, is spent AFTER the daily quota and the redeem/gift bonuses of an extension (so a free booster is never wasted by a purchase), and - unlike the daily allowance - is NOT cleared by the daily reset: it was paid for.

boosterRender._comment: Rendering of the 3D booster (js/UI/components/Booster3DRenderer.js). 'defaultMode' is the mode a new account starts at and the one used when the stored preference is unknown; 'modes' lists every selectable rendering, in the order the developer settings screen shows them. Each mode carries the full lighting/material recipe: 'exposure' (tone mapping), 'environmentIntensity' (strength of the studio reflections on the materials), the four/five light intensities ('ambient', 'key', 'rim', 'front', 'hemisphere'), the PBR values 'metalness' and 'roughness', the clearcoat layer of a blister plastic ('clearcoat' and 'clearcoatRoughness', 0 disables it), 'emissive' (self-lighting taken from the texture) and 'normalScale' (multiplier applied to the normal map baked in the .glb). A missing value falls back to the classic recipe and an out-of-range value is clamped, so a partial edit never breaks the scene. The render picker is only shown in the settings screen when the developer mode is enabled.

minePick._comment: Mine Pick. The daily board holds 'boosterCount' SIMULATED openings, built from the real booster parameters: 'boosters.cardsPerBooster', the rarity table of each extension (which may override 'defaultRarity.json') and 'boosters.godpackChancePercent'. A simulated pack is therefore drawn exactly like an opened one. 'picksPerDay' free picks per UTC day (reset at midnight UTC, like the daily boosters), 'historySize' picks kept for the statistics. The board is deterministic: it is seeded with 'seedSalt' + the UTC day + the account UUID, so a reload shows the same board, it changes at the next UTC day, and two accounts never share one (changing 'seedSalt' rebuilds the board of the CURRENT day, and the boosters already picked become stale). The extension of each booster is drawn at random with a weight of (rank + 1) ** 'setWeightExponent': the extension whose id ranks highest is the most likely.

mining._comment: Mine (MineBlock). The rules of the blocks themselves - the five kinds, their 'Weight' (the chance of falling on one), their 'Hardness' (the number of taps needed to break one) and their loot (a guaranteed 'dust', sometimes 'Sparks') - live in 'configPath', so the mine can be rebalanced without touching this file. 'blocksPerDay' blocks are offered every UTC day (reset at midnight UTC, like the daily boosters and the Mine Pick) and they are mined ONE BY ONE: the next block is only drawn once the previous one is broken. The order of the day is seeded with 'seedSalt' + the UTC day + the account UUID, so a reload resumes the very block that was being mined and two accounts never share the same sequence. 'nextBlockDelayMs' is how long the broken block stays on screen before the next one drops in (the rewards keep flying while it does): a small value keeps the mining fast, a large one lets the loot be admired.

promos._comment: Promo cards. 'directory' holds one file per series ('A1.json' -> the 'A1-Promo' group), an entry being a card built exactly like a booster card ('Index', 'Name_XX', 'Desc_XX', 'Rarity', 'Style', 'Layout', 'Path'). Promo cards are NEVER drawn from a booster: they only enter the collection through a redeem code or a gift, only appear in the collection when they are owned, and never count in a completion ratio. 'sets' lists the files to load; leave it empty to load one file per booster extension of 'boosters.sets'. A series without a promo file simply has no promo.

timeSync.comment: Providers are tried in order. 'format' tells DateSyncManager how to read the payload: json (object), trace (key=value lines), headers (HTTP response headers). Order is driven by browser reachability: a provider without Access-Control-Allow-Origin cannot be read from a page. See js/business/DateSyncManager.js.

sparks._comment: Sparks currency. 'sellPrice'/'buyPrice' map a rarity (1-5) to its value in Sparks; 'boosterReward' is credited on every booster opening. Every key falls back to its built-in default when absent.

useritemCode._comment: Step 10 personal codes. 'key' is 32 random bytes in base64 ('openssl rand -base64 32'); the value below is a PLACEHOLDER (32 zero bytes) that MUST be replaced, with the same value in the game master generator. WARNING: this key is served to the browser, so anyone reading the sources can forge codes (see .docs/gamemaster/useritemcode.md section 2).

levelling._comment: the default level is 'defaultLevel'. To level up the first level, you need 'baseRequiredExpToLevelUp' XP, and each level, the requirement increase by 'incrementRequiredXpBy' XP. 'experience' is the XP earned from the account itself: every booster opened, every distinct card of the collection, and a custom player name (not 'profile.defaultName').

ExperiencePerTrophy._comment: Trophies gives thoses experience with thoses rarity. Except if it's explicitly said in the trophy json

trophies._comment: Trophy catalogue. 'boostersConfigPath' holds the tiers recurring on every extension (completion + opened boosters), 'globalConfigPath' the account wide tiers, and 'directory' one file per extension (<setId>.json) listing the collection trophies. The XP of a trophy comes from 'ExperiencePerTrophy', unless its JSON declares its own 'Experience'.

profile._comment: Player profile. 'maxFavorites' and 'maxFeaturedTrophies' are the absolute number of slots of each pin list, 'defaultFavorites' and 'defaultFeaturedTrophies' the slots every new account starts with, and the two price maps the Sparks cost of each additional slot (keys are slot numbers). A slot can only be bought in order: the next one after the slots the account owns. 'defaultName' is the name that does NOT grant the 'nameChanged' experience (empty = any typed name counts).

profileIcons._comment: Profile avatars. 'defaultPath' lists the icons every account can select from the start, 'unlockablePath' the icons that a trophy unlocks (matched by name), and 'directory' holds one <setId>.json per extension mapping a collection trophy name to the icons it unlocks.

titles._comment: Player titles (the line under the pseudo). 'defaultPath' lists the titles unlocked by LEVEL - one entry per title, with its 'requiredLevel' and its 'text' per language - and 'directory' holds one <setId>.json per extension mapping a collection trophy name to the titles it unlocks (the titles are written in the file itself, unlike the icons, which share the trophy of an extension). A title is designated by its 'id' everywhere: a save only ever stores that id.

profileCard._comment: Profile card (section 3.G octies): the trading card the profile page draws from the account with the card maker of 'external/cardmakerz/'. 'rarityThresholds' maps a card rarity (1 = Commune ... 5 = Mythique, the rarity scale of the card data) to the NUMBER OF UNLOCKED TROPHIES it takes to reach it; the card takes the highest rarity whose threshold the account reaches, so a brand new account is Commune. A threshold that is missing, malformed or LOWER than the previous one falls back to the shipped value (the sequence can never make a rarer card easier). 'defaultArtPath' is the illustration used as the card background when the player has no favourite card to borrow one from. 'seriesDigits' is how many last characters of the account UUID the series line prints after the player title.

cardDetail._comment: Interactive card details. Every detail dialog of the game (collection, profile favourite, Wandering Trader offer, opening summary, statistics history, shared binder) lets the player grab the card and tilt it. 'maxRotationDeg' is the maximum angle in degrees on each axis (the drag is clamped to it, 45 at most); 'thicknessPx' is the visible thickness of the cardstock, drawn as a slight edge behind the card (24 px at most). 'enabled: false' turns the interaction off everywhere and leaves plain pictures. Both values are read once per page, so changing them needs no code change; a value outside its range is clamped, never rejected.

features._comment: Extra features bought with Sparks (see `js/business/FeatureManager.js`). Each entry of 'items' is one purchasable feature, under the identifier the code knows it by: 'cardLayoutFullArt' locks the Full Art layout of the profile card. 'priceSparks' is what it costs, a whole number of Sparks. An entry the code knows (see `FeatureManager.FEATURES`) falls back to its shipped price when the value here is missing, negative or malformed, so a typo can never give a paid feature away; an entry nobody knows is ignored rather than sold blind. Buying is final: there is no refund, which is why the price is shown before the confirmation.

shop._comment: Wandering Trader (the trading screen of the Mine, `js/business/TraderManager.js`). Four kinds of offers. THE WEEKLY SHOP is drawn from a seed built on the date of the MONDAY of the current week and nothing else - no account, no device: every player sees the same cards at the same price, and the shop rerolls by itself every Monday at 00:00 UTC ('seedSalt' changes the draw for everyone, and rebuilds the CURRENT week). 'offers' is its composition (rarity -> how many cards, pooled from every loaded extension, never twice the same card). A card is paid in exactly three kinds of mined resource, and 'rarityValues' (what a card of that rarity is worth) and 'itemsValues' (what one unit of a resource is worth) are read in the same unit, so the price of a card is always worth its rarity to the unit - a name in 'itemsValues' that matches no reward of 'settings/mining.json' can never be asked for. 'allItemsUniques' decides whether an offer can be bought again once it was bought: true, it is exhausted until the next reroll; false, the shop sells it as long as the player has the resources. THE PINNED OFFERS are hand-written in 'pinnedPath' (card, price, days it is sold in and stock, see the file itself): they are never random and always open the shop. THE DAILY TRADES are 'tradesPerDay' resource-for-resource swaps drawn from the UTC DAY alone (same trades for everyone, new ones at midnight UTC): the dearest side counts 1 unit and the cheapest one as many units as 'itemsValues' asks for (1 Ultima against 2 Void Dust), so a trade is always worth the same on both sides and can be taken in either direction, once per day. A pair whose values are not a multiple of one another (Glowstone Dust at 20 against Void Dust at 50) has no such exchange and is never drawn. THE DAILY SPARKS OFFER ('dailySparkOffer') draws one resource and a quantity whose total value never exceeds 'maxResourceValue'; it is sold once a day for 'priceMultiplier' times that value, in Sparks. Both numbers are read on every render, so the economy is tuned here.

dailySparkOffer._comment: One resource sold for Sparks per UTC day, once. Its quantity is drawn so that quantity * its value in 'itemsValues' never exceeds 'maxResourceValue'; 'priceMultiplier' turns that value into the price in Sparks (2 = the player pays twice the value).
